Each rule of this spec is proven by tests that carry its code (a tag, a title, a comment).

| Propriedade | Valor |
| --- | --- |
| Julgamento | uma IA ou uma pessoa responde a pergunta abaixo, via `anchors judge` |
| Confronta | `spec` |
| Bloqueante por padrão — projeto novo | sim |
| Bloqueante por padrão — projeto existente | não — informa |

## A pergunta

> Each rule of this spec is proven by tests that carry its code (a tag, a title, a comment). For each rule, read its text and what those tests ASSERT — the targets of their expect/assert, the functions, tables, fields and values they check — and answer: does what the tests assert agree with what the rule says? Fail it when the rule names one thing and the test asserts another (the rule records the item in one place, the test expects a call that writes another), when the test asserts the opposite of the rule, or when the rule names variants and the tests carrying it prove only some. Agreement in other words is a pass. For each contradiction, name the rule, the test (file:line) and both sides, and say which one is wrong if the spec or the code tells. BEFORE ANSWERING, check whether this unit declares `@TBD` for the piece this question asks about (`@TBD: code`, `@TBD: code,test`, …). If it does, the test does NOT exist yet by a recorded decision, and there is nothing to confront: answer `waived`, naming the absence ("the spec declares @TBD for this piece and it does not exist in the repository"). Do NOT answer `pass` — `pass` is a statement ABOUT the test, and without the test it states what nobody verified; the stamp stays in the map looking like real verification. Also check that the `@TBD` is TRUE: if the piece already exists in the repository, the marker is stale, the judgment is due as usual, and the stale declaration is a finding — while it stays there, every gate that reads it waives what it should demand.

## Como declarar

```yaml
gates:
  - name: rule-test-coherent
    on: [spec]
    measures: judgment
```
